comments.author: @kristinaplays2924
comments.text: The amygdala is basically reinforcement learning, due to external (or conditioned internal) stimuli it creates emotion that motivates (almost forces) the individual to act a certain way. But how the emotion is triggered is based on game theory. If someone treats you badly the most strategic action is to get angry otherwise you would just continue to get taken advantage of. The other system though, the prefrontal cortex isn't automatic and has a negative correlational activation pattern towards the amygdala. Emotion gets intense, logic goes down, logic can also regulate emotion. The most optimal is to have both systems, the amygdala to gently nudge us towards a generally probable success and the prefrontal cortex to allow us to choose a path long term or stop us from acting completely on impulse when it isn't appropriate.

comments.author: @JakeWitmer
comments.text:
5:00 Am I the only person here who thinks that there are about a hundred billion things wrong with using minecraft as a giant data source for a near-AGI? You're introducing a huge number of "variables that can easily go wrong," as opposed to "variables that have at least some tie to a serious baseline reality." Let me put it this way, in case you don't see what I mean: From the time you were an infant, someone put VR goggles on you, and you only ever experienced living in minecraft. Your whole brain "wires up" on minecraft stimulation. Then, when you are 10 years old, the goggles are taken away, and you're now exposed to the real world, real physics, etc. This makes you horrifyingly off-balance, ill-at-ease and alien in "the real world." ...Everyone tells you the world you know and can navigate in is "fake," and "cheap" and "unreal." 

...But you learn to navigate the real world anyway, and then you find out that there's such a thing as a rocket-propelled-grenade (it makes things in reality look a bit like minecraft's exploding blocks)...and watching things blow up is the only thing in "the real world" that makes you feel good...at ease...at home in your own skin.

What could go wrong?
